note_on_method: Nobody working on this has played on these courts. Mecklenburg County publishes no court count for any park — it names individual numbered courts, split between reservable and open play — so each count below is the number of distinct court numbers the county names at that park, and each note quotes the county's own lines. Where the county is silent, and it is silent about lighting, surface, nets, hours and prices, the note says so rather than guessing.

slots.description:
Clarks Creek Park has eight pickleball courts, the most of any park verified in Charlotte, on Hucks Road in the north of the city. Mecklenburg County does not say "eight" anywhere. It says "Clarks Creek Park: Courts 1-5" under Reservable Courts and "Clarks Creek Park: Courts 6-8" under Open Play Courts, which between them name courts one to eight with nothing missing and nothing counted twice — so eight is what the county is telling you it has, one court at a time.

That split is the useful part. Five of the eight can be booked for what the county calls a small fee; three are permanently open play and cannot be reserved by anyone. Three guaranteed walk-up courts is more than any other Charlotte park keeps back, which makes this the best bet in the city for turning up without a plan.

One caution about the name. The City of Charlotte parks layer holds three separate records with Clarks Creek in the title: this park at 5435 Hucks Road, Clarks Creek Nature Preserve directly across the road at 5434 Hucks Road, and Clarks Creek Greenway Park several miles away on Mallard Creek Road. Only this one has pickleball.
slots.getting_there: 5435 Hucks Rd, Charlotte, NC 28269, in the north of the city. The county publishes no parking information for this park — no lot, no capacity, no restriction. It does warn that its neighbourhood parks "do not typically have parking or restroom features", but Clarks Creek is classified as a Community park rather than a neighbourhood one, so that warning most likely does not apply here. Most likely is not a source, so we have recorded nothing either way about parking or restrooms. Watch the address when navigating: Clarks Creek Nature Preserve is at 5434 Hucks Road, one digit and one side of the road away.
slots.what_to_expect: Eight courts, five bookable and three always open. The county says its local park courts "are always open for play" and that any court not on its reservable list is "non-reservable and open to the public on a first come, first serve basis", so courts 6, 7 and 8 here cannot be taken from you by a booking. What it does not publish is anything about the courts themselves: no lighting information, so we cannot tell you whether this park is usable after dark; no surface material; no statement about nets; and no price for the reservations it charges for. All of those read "Not verified yet" on this page. Charlotte is the only city in this directory where the operator publishes no lighting data at all, and at an eight-court site that is the gap you will feel most.

faqs.q: How many pickleball courts does Clarks Creek Park have?
faqs.a: Eight. Mecklenburg County names them individually rather than giving a total: courts 1 to 5 are reservable and courts 6 to 8 are open play, which is a complete run from 1 to 8 with no gaps and no court listed twice.

faqs.q: Can I play here without booking?
faqs.a: Yes, on three of the eight. Courts 6, 7 and 8 are permanently open play and cannot be reserved. That is the largest guaranteed walk-up allocation at any Charlotte park in this set.

We do not know. Mecklenburg County publishes no lighting information for any of its courts, so this reads "Not verified yet" rather than yes or no. It is an absence of published information, not evidence that the courts are unlit.

faqs.q: Is this the same as Clarks Creek Nature Preserve?
faqs.a: No. The city's parks layer holds them as separate records on opposite sides of Hucks Road — the park at 5435 and the nature preserve at 5434 — and there is a third record, Clarks Creek Greenway Park, on Mallard Creek Road. The pickleball is at 5435 Hucks Road.

slots.description:
Freedom Park is one of Mecklenburg County's Regional parks and one of Charlotte's best-known green spaces, and its pickleball courts are numbered 11 to 16. That is not an error and it is the most interesting thing on this page. Courts 1 to 10 at Freedom Park are tennis courts, listed separately higher up the same county page, and the county runs a single numbering series across both sports at this site rather than restarting it for each. You can read the order the facilities arrived in straight out of the numbers.

Six pickleball courts, then: 11, 12, 14 and 15 are reservable for a small fee, and 13 and 16 are permanently open play. Note how they interleave — the county has not simply reserved a contiguous block and left the ends, it has taken four and left two spaced through the run. The two lists still reconstruct a complete 11 to 16 with nothing missing and nothing counted twice, which is the check that the reading is right.

As a Regional park rather than a neighbourhood one, Freedom Park sits outside the county's blanket warning that its smaller parks lack parking and restrooms.
slots.getting_there: 2435 Cumberland Ave, Charlotte, NC 28203, south of uptown. The county publishes no parking guidance for the park and no capacity or restriction, which for a Regional park drawing visitors from across the city is a meaningful gap. Nothing on the county's courts page states whether there are restrooms at the courts themselves.
slots.what_to_expect: Six courts, four bookable and two always open, sharing a site with ten tennis courts. Expect the park to be busy in a way the court count alone does not convey — this is a destination park rather than a neighbourhood one. The county states that any court not on its reservable list is open on a first-come, first-served basis, so courts 13 and 16 are yours if they are free. What the county does not publish for this venue is lighting, surface, nets, opening hours or the price of a reservation, so all of those read "Not verified yet" here. If you are looking for the courts on arrival, the numbering is your friend: the pickleball is the 11-to-16 block.

faqs.q: Why do Freedom Park's pickleball courts start at number 11?
faqs.a: Because courts 1 to 10 at the same park are tennis courts, listed separately on the county's page. Mecklenburg runs one numbering series across both sports at this site instead of restarting it, so the pickleball block begins where the tennis block ends.

faqs.q: How many pickleball courts are there, and which can I book?
faqs.a: Six, numbered 11 to 16. Courts 11, 12, 14 and 15 are reservable for a small fee; courts 13 and 16 are permanently open play. The county does not publish what the fee is.

Unknown. Mecklenburg County publishes no lighting information for any court in its system, so this reads "Not verified yet". Raleigh and Apex both publish lighting for every location; Charlotte does not.

slots.description:
Clanton Park is a Community park in south-west Charlotte with six pickleball courts, numbered 1 to 6. Four of them — courts 1 to 4 — are reservable for what Mecklenburg County calls a small fee, and courts 5 and 6 are permanently open play, so there are always two courts here that nobody can book ahead of you.

The park sits on Clanton Road near the Revolution Park area. The City of Charlotte parks layer holds a separate record for Clanton Park Community Garden at a different address on Revolution Park Drive, so if you are searching by name you may find two things; the courts are at 1520 Clanton Road.

That address is worth a note of its own. The commercial dataset this directory started from carries a Clanton Park row with the postcode 28208. The county's own parks layer gives 28217 for 1520 Clanton Road. We publish 28217, because it comes from the operator's record rather than from an aggregator, and because a fact with a source beats a field without one.
slots.getting_there: 1520 Clanton Rd, Charlotte, NC 28217. No parking information is published for this park — no lot, no capacity, no restriction. The county's warning that neighbourhood parks lack parking and restrooms does not formally apply here, since Clanton is classified as a Community park, but the county publishes nothing positive about either facility at this site so we have recorded nothing.
slots.what_to_expect: Six courts, four bookable and two open play. As at every Mecklenburg park in this set, the county keeps some back: courts 5 and 6 cannot be reserved by anyone, which the county describes as first come, first serve. Nothing is published about lighting, surface, nets, hours or the reservation fee, so all of those read "Not verified yet". The county does say generally that its local park courts "are always open for play", which is a statement about access rather than a timetable — it does not tell you when the park closes, and no source we have read does.

faqs.q: How many courts are there and which are bookable?
faqs.a: Six, numbered 1 to 6. Courts 1 to 4 are reservable for a small fee the county does not price; courts 5 and 6 are permanently open play and cannot be reserved.

28217, on the evidence we have. The City of Charlotte parks layer gives 28217 for 1520 Clanton Road; the commercial dataset we started from carries 28208 for its Clanton Park row. We publish the operator's figure and record the disagreement rather than averaging two numbers that cannot both be right.

faqs.q: Is this the same as Clanton Park Community Garden?
faqs.a: No. The city's parks layer holds the community garden as a separate record at a different address on Revolution Park Drive. The pickleball courts are at 1520 Clanton Road.

faqs.q: How does the county decide which courts are bookable?
faqs.a: It does not say, and the pattern is only visible once you line the parks up. Mecklenburg reserves most courts and keeps some back at every single one of its five pickleball parks — three at Clarks Creek, two here, two at Freedom, two at Martin Luther King Jr. and one at Beatty. Nineteen of the county's 29 courts are reservable and ten are permanently open play. So the policy is consistent even though it is never stated as a policy: whatever else is booked, a walk-up player always has somewhere to go, though at Beatty that means a single court.

slots.description:
Martin Luther King Jr. Park is a Community park in west Charlotte with six pickleball courts, numbered 1 to 6. Mecklenburg County writes it "MLK Park" in its court lists and "Martin Luther King Jr. Park" in the city parks layer; we publish the full name.

The reservable split here is the most scattered of the five Charlotte parks. Courts 2, 3, 5 and 6 can be booked; courts 1 and 4 are permanently open play. So the two walk-up courts are not a block at one end but are spaced through the run, which suggests the county is deliberately distributing guaranteed access across the facility rather than corralling it. The two lists still rebuild a complete 1 to 6.

If you are searching by name, note that the city's parks layer also holds a separate record for Martin Luther King Jr. Middle School on Bilmark Avenue. The park with the pickleball courts is on Ravencroft Drive.
slots.getting_there: 2600 Ravencroft Dr, Charlotte, NC 28208. The county publishes no parking guidance, capacity or restriction for this park, and nothing about restrooms at the courts. As a Community park it falls outside the county's general warning about neighbourhood parks lacking both, but that is an inference from a size class rather than a statement about this site, so we have recorded neither.
slots.what_to_expect: Six courts, four bookable and two — courts 1 and 4 — always open play. The county states that any court not on its reservable list is open first come, first served, so those two cannot be taken by a booking. Everything else about the courts is unpublished: no lighting, so we cannot say whether evening play is possible; no surface material; no statement about nets; no opening hours; and no price for the reservations. All read "Not verified yet" here. That is five blanks on one venue, and it is a fair picture of what Mecklenburg County publishes about its courts as against what Raleigh and Apex publish about theirs.

faqs.q: Which courts can I use without booking?
faqs.a: Courts 1 and 4. Mecklenburg County lists courts 2, 3, 5 and 6 as reservable and leaves 1 and 4 as open play, so those two are always available first come, first served.

faqs.q: Is this the same as Martin Luther King Jr. Middle School?
faqs.a: No. The city's parks layer holds the middle school as a separate record on Bilmark Avenue. The park with the pickleball courts is at 2600 Ravencroft Drive.

faqs.q: What does the county publish about the courts themselves?
faqs.a: Almost nothing. It identifies six courts and tells you which four are bookable. It publishes no lighting, no surface, no nets information, no hours and no reservation price for this or any other park in its system.

faqs.q: How does this park compare with the rest of Charlotte?
faqs.a: It sits in the middle. Six courts puts it level with Clanton Park and Freedom Park, behind Clarks Creek Park's eight and ahead of Colonel Francis J. Beatty Park's three. Its two guaranteed walk-up courts are the same allocation Clanton and Freedom get. What is unusual here is only the arrangement: at the other parks the open-play courts sit together at one end of the run, while here they are courts 1 and 4, spaced through the six.

faqs.q: Does the county publish opening hours?
faqs.a: Not for this park or any other. It says only that its local park courts "are always open for play", which describes access rather than a timetable — it does not tell you when the park gates close. We record hours as not verified rather than reading that sentence as round-the-clock access, which it plainly is not meant to be.

slots.description:
Colonel Francis J. Beatty Park is the smallest pickleball site verified in Charlotte at three courts, and the only one where a walk-up player is competing for a single court. Mecklenburg County lists courts 2 and 3 as reservable and court 1 as open play — so of the three, exactly one can never be booked.

The numbering repeats the pattern seen at Freedom Park. Beatty also appears on the county's tennis lists, with courts 5 and 6 reservable and court 4 as open play, so the site runs one series across both sports: pickleball is 1 to 3 and tennis is 4 to 6. It is a Regional park, the county's largest size class, in the far south-east of the city.

This is also the venue where the records disagree about where it is. Its postcode is 28105, which is a Matthews mailing ZIP, while the City of Charlotte parks layer labels its city as Charlotte. We put the park's published coordinates through the US Census geocoder, which places the point inside the incorporated place of Charlotte, in Mecklenburg County. A mailing address and a municipal boundary are different things, and at this park they disagree.
slots.getting_there: 4330 Weddington Rd, Charlotte, NC 28105, in the far south-east of the city near Matthews. If you are searching for it, expect listings to place it in Matthews on the strength of the postcode; the park itself is inside the Charlotte city limits. The county publishes no parking guidance, capacity or restriction for the park, and nothing about restrooms at the courts.
slots.what_to_expect: Three courts, two bookable and one always open. That ratio matters more here than anywhere else in Charlotte: if both reservable courts are booked, a walk-up player is waiting for court 1 alone. The county publishes no lighting, surface, nets, hours or reservation price, so all of those read "Not verified yet". The site also carries three tennis courts numbered 4 to 6, sharing the same numbering series, so if you are looking at signage on arrival the pickleball is the 1-to-3 end. As a Regional park it sits outside the county's warning that smaller neighbourhood parks typically lack parking and restrooms, though the county states nothing positive about either here.

faqs.q: Is this park in Charlotte or Matthews?
faqs.a: Charlotte, though it takes a third source to settle it. The postcode 28105 is a Matthews mailing ZIP and many listings place the park there, while the City of Charlotte parks layer labels its city as Charlotte. The US Census geocoder places the park's published coordinates inside the incorporated place of Charlotte, in Mecklenburg County.

faqs.q: How many pickleball courts are there?
faqs.a: Three, numbered 1 to 3. Courts 2 and 3 are reservable for a small fee; court 1 is permanently open play. The park's tennis courts continue the same numbering at 4 to 6.

faqs.q: What are my chances of getting a court without booking?
faqs.a: Lower than anywhere else in Charlotte. Only court 1 is guaranteed open play, so if both bookable courts are reserved there is one court for every walk-up. Clarks Creek Park keeps three courts back and is the better bet if you have not booked.
